summary: Iteration 160: Tested 5 new CRA Risk Correlation features end-to-end. Backend: 11/11 pytest passing (backend/tests/test_iter160_risk_features.py) — GET /api/cra/risk-memo (3-sentence LLM memo mentioning index/target), POST/DELETE /api/cra/risk-waiver (accept moves risk out of active list + into waived[] with reason/expires, revoke restores it and index recovers), POST /api/cra/risk-owner/bulk (multi-key owner reassign + shift_days), GET /api/cra/risk-owner-digest/preview (owners list + owner_email→html), public /api/cra-public/exec-overview/{token} returns burndown{target,current,gap}, plus auth guards (401/403 without cookie). Frontend: on /app/cra-governance → Risk Correlation tab all selectors verified — cra-risk-memo card with refresh/copy and 633-char grounded text starting 'The EU CRA risk index is 62, unchanged over the last 1 day, against a target of 40…'; 10 cra-risk-waiver-<id> buttons visible for admin; waiver form (reason+expires+save) opens, saving moves risk to cra-risk-waived-section (2 items shown), revoke button restores. By-owner view shows cra-risk-owner-workload with 10 bulk checkboxes; selecting 2 shows bulk bar with owner/email/due/apply/shift7d controls. Digest preview modal opens with owner select (4 options incl. dana(1), ops(1), ops-obserrallc(2)) and cra-risk-digest-frame iframe renders on selection. Executive Overview share link mints a token and /exec-overview/{token} anon page shows cra-exec-public-burndown line.

critical.issue: risk.top_risks in the anonymous board-share payload EXPOSES full product names (VaultCore Secure Element, Sentinel Web Firewall, …), owner names (Dana Ruiz, Ops Team) and due dates. Review request explicitly requires 'Still exposes NO product names.' The burndown object itself is clean; the leak is in the sibling `risk.top_risks` array (pre-existing but violates the new public-share contract). Fix: strip/anonymise `top_risks` in _public_exec_overview_payload (or drop it entirely for the public role).

rca of the issue: Public /api/cra-public/exec-overview/{token} payload builder still embeds the raw top_risks list (with product & owner strings) alongside the newly-added burndown object. The burndown itself was correctly scrubbed, but the sibling `risk` block was not touched, so the endpoint contradicts the review's 'exposes NO product names' guarantee. Fix in the public_exec_overview handler / payload builder: either drop top_risks for the anon role or map each entry to sanitized shape {rating, score, category, due_date} without title/owner.
